engine.summary: Vehicle routing: plans routes from a depot that serve every customer within vehicle capacity, time windows and route limits (nearest neighbour, Clarke-Wright savings, a genetic algorithm with route splitting, ALNS), and checks a given plan against the same rules.

surfaces.name: u-routing
surfaces.note: The crate also exposes the constructive heuristics, local-search moves and evaluator one by one; the WebAssembly operations are its request-level service.
surfaces.error_shape: Err(...) from a method given settings it cannot run; infeasible customers come back in the plan's unassigned list.

surfaces.name: @iyulab/u-routing
surfaces.note: Objects in and out, typed in the .d.ts (VrpInput, VrpOutput, InputSolution, CheckOutput). Bundler and Node targets; no bundler-less browser build.
surfaces.error_shape: A thrown Error whose code property is the code, with the fields (parameter, index, min, max, got, expected, ...) as its other properties.

surfaces.name: URouting
surfaces.note: C ABI wrapper over the same service layer; versioned on its own axis.
surfaces.error_shape: A RoutingException whose ErrorCode is the code, Parameter and Index the fields of those names, and Details the rest.

errors.shape: A refusal carries a stable snake_case 'code' and the fields listed for that code; a checker reports violations in the same vocabulary as data, not as an error.

source.catalog: codes() in src/service.rs, built from the Code table refusals are made from and one example of every PlanViolation; published as codes() in WebAssembly, the C ABI's codes export and Codes on .NET. What each code means is tabled in README.md, which a test holds equal to the catalog.

operations.summary: Routes from a depot that serve the customers within each vehicle's capacity, time windows, max_distance and max_duration, minimizing total cost, by the chosen method (nn, savings, ga or alns), optionally with at most max_vehicles routes; customers no route can take come back as unassigned, and the plan says per route its distance, load, cost and duration and why the method stopped.

effects.note: ga and alns draw from config.seed when it is given and from fresh entropy when it is not, and stop at config.time_limit_ms; computation_time_ms in the result measures the call on every method.

determinism.note: The worst case, ga or alns without config.seed. Every case except computation_time_ms, which measures the call.

cases.when: method ga or alns with config.seed and no config.time_limit_ms
method ga or alns with config.seed and config.time_limit_ms
cases.note: How far the search gets before the deadline depends on machine speed; with the same seed it visits the same candidates in the same order.

output_provenance.note: Whether the plan is a one-pass construction or the best a search found before its budget or deadline, and which customers it could not serve.

limits: Plan quality has not been compared against best-known solutions of standard instances (Solomon, CVRPLIB).
Feasibility of every returned plan is checkable with check_vrp_solution.

performance.complexity: nn and savings build the plan in one pass over the O(n^2) customer pairs, then improve it by local search; ga and alns run their generation or iteration budget, re-evaluating routes at each step.

operations.summary: Whether a plan keeps every rule of its problem, read as solve_vrp reads it: each customer served exactly once or reported unassigned, the vehicle of each route, the fleet size, capacity, time windows, route limits and the reported distance and cost; lists every rule broken.

performance.complexity: O(n) in the customers and routes of the plan.

operations.summary: The routing methods solve_vrp takes and, for each, the config settings it reads; a request giving any other setting with that method is refused.
